transcript.content: hey, i'm berry. tell me a dream, however it comes back to you.

oh hey berry. ok so the bit i keep seeing is the colours—everything was super bright and glowing, like neon signs at night, but against grey dusty ground. it was a night market on the moon? people just walking around in normal clothes, no spacesuits, like that was nothing.
a night market on the moon — i like that nobody thinks twice about it. the neon on grey dust is so vivid. what were the signs saying?
i don't actually remember any signs with words on them, sorry. it was more just glowing colours everywhere—pinks and blues and greens. and the earth was huge and blue in the black sky above.
no need to be sorry, dreams are like that. the earth just hanging there, huge and blue — that must have looked amazing over all those colours.

yeah, it was. the stalls were in rows on the grey dust, all lit up, and earth was just there, massive and blue against the black. paper lanterns were floating up from the stalls too, just drifting straight up into the sky.
lanterns lifting off into all that black, with the earth watching. was it busy — like crowds of people around you, or more spaced out?

it was pretty busy, yeah. lots of people in ordinary clothes, roaming between the rows of stalls. but also every step was like a huge slow jump, so everything felt sort of floaty and spread out even with the crowd.
floaty crowds, people nearly drifting into each other with those big slow steps. what did you do while you were there?
my best friend priya was with me. she bought two bowls of noodles from a stall run by a robot—a tall thin silver one with a round head. the bowls were glowing too.
priya and a robot, glowing noodles — that's so specific. did you eat them?

i don't remember eating them, no. i remember we started jumping, higher and higher, using those floaty steps, both of us laughing. we got above the stalls, up where the lanterns were. that's the last thing i remember.
the two of you above the market, up with the lanterns and the earth. that's a lovely place for a dream to leave off. how did you feel, up there?
free, mostly. like it was easy and funny, not scary at all. just bouncing higher and laughing with priya, and the lanterns sort of drifting around us.
easy and funny — it sounds it. of all of it, what's the moment that still stays with you most?

the jump, i think. that feeling of going higher and higher without trying, and priya right there, both of us laughing. but the colours under us—the neon stalls against the grey dust—that's the image i can't shake.
so, of everything in that dream — the robot, the lanterns, the noodles, priya — was there any one thing that mattered most? or did nothing in particular stand out?
i'd say priya. not that the other stuff didn't matter, but having her there, doing the same floaty jumps and laughing, that's what made it feel so good. the dream would've been lonely without her.
that's clear. and of all that — the glowing stalls, the big blue earth, the floaty jumps — which bit felt most dreamlike to you?
the earth, honestly. just hanging there huge and blue and quiet over all that noise and colour. it should've been scary or wrong, but it just felt normal in a dreamy way.
yeah, the earth was huge and blue, normal in that dreamy way. i asked because i wanted to catch the odd details, not because anything felt missing.
ah ok. yeah, the oddest thing was probably how nobody questioned it. no suits, no panic, just people shopping on the moon with the earth up there like an advert.

so you were at a night market on the moon, with neon colours everywhere against grey dust, and the earth hanging huge and blue in the black sky. it was busy but floaty, people in normal clothes with no suits, every step like a big slow jump. priya was with you. she bought two glowing bowls of noodles from a tall silver robot. you started jumping higher and higher, both laughing, up past the stalls to where the lanterns were, feeling free and easy. the part that stays with you is that jump, going up without trying, with priya right there, and the image of the neon stalls against the grey dust. priya is what mattered most — it would have been lonely without her. and the earth felt the most dreamlike, big and quiet and normal in that dreamy way.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
you got it right. only thing is the glowing noodles were in glowing bowls—that detail stuck. but yeah, other than that, that's exactly how it was.
got it — glowing noodles in glowing bowls. i'll hold onto that.
yeah, the bowls made it extra weird. like each one had its own little light under the grey dust.
that little light under the grey dust — yeah, that's a nice odd touch.
it's the kind of thing you only notice in a dream. like it's totally normal until you tell someone and they look at you funny.

exactly. and that's part of why i love hearing them.

thank you for sharing this one with me, it was a lovely thing to picture.
